🌐 Bitcoin spam fight escalates as Dashjr backs BIP-110 

🔖 Bitcoin developer Luke Dashjr has rejected calls to withdraw BIP-110, a disputed proposal that aims to limit non-financial data on Bitcoin. The proposal has renewed debate over whether the network should only process money transfers or also support data-heavy uses such as Ordinals and Runes. Dashjr wrote, “Saylor didn’t say anything about BIP110.” He added, “And no, it’s too late to cancel BIP110.” His comment came after fresh debate around Michael Saylor’s view that Bitcoin should change slowly and protect its core design.

⚠️ BIP-110, also called the Reduced Data Temporary Softfork, seeks to place temporary limits on certain forms of arbitrary data in Bitcoin transactions. The proposal’s text says it aims to move Bitcoin back toward “the world’s money” by rejecting data storage as a supported use case at the consensus level. The dispute centers on block space. Supporters of BIP-110 argue that inscriptions, Runes and other data-heavy activity raise storage demands and push Bitcoin away from peer-to-peer payments. 

📣 Critics argue that Bitcoin block space should remain open to any user willing to pay the required fee. They say attempts to restrict transaction content could create a harmful precedent and split users over subjective rules. The debate also followed Michael Saylor’s latest comments on Bitcoin’s role. Saylor said Bitcoin is not a technology stock, payments company, or software platform competing to add features.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Akbar Ghasemi, the new ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Vietnam, presented his credentials to President To Lam on Monday.

During the meeting with the new Iranian ambassador, the Vietnamese president described Iran as a country with a magnificent civilization and rich history. To Lam called for stronger bilateral economic cooperation as the main pillar of mutual relations, alongside the further development of cultural, educational, and tourism collaboration.
​
To Lam stated that his 2023 visit to Iran opened a new chapter in bilateral relations, adding that Hanoi is fully prepared to deepen mutual cooperation across all fields.
​
He also welcomed the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding between Iran and the United States, expressing hope that this process would bring greater stability and peace to various regions of the world.
​
For his part, the Iranian ambassador pointed out the diverse capacities and extensive capabilities of both nations. He said that following the recent developments, the geopolitical and strategic position of Iran has significantly elevated, doubling the potential for cooperation between Tehran and Hanoi in all sectors.
​
Ghasemi also affirmed that Iran stands ready to expand political, economic, parliamentary, commercial, technological, tourism, and cultural cooperation with Vietnam.

The world’s largest funds are changing their strategy

Every year, Invesco publishes one of the most important surveys in the global economy.

They sit down with dozens of the world’s largest institutional funds and central banks and ask one simple question: what are you actually planning to do?

Together, they manage $29 trillion in assets. That’s more than the annual GDP of the United States. In practice, these are the institutions that determine what happens in global markets.

And this time, they surprised a lot of economists:

• 80% of them named energy infrastructure as their top priority for the years ahead: almost all are investing in power generation, electricity grids, LNG, and nuclear energy.

• Another 33% plan to significantly increase their gold holdings. More importantly, they want to store that gold within their own countries rather than with U.S. custodians. Several central banks are already building alternative asset storage systems outside the United States.

• At the same time, the share of central banks expecting the U.S. dollar’s global role to weaken has risen from 12% to 29% in just two years. Nearly a threefold increase.

The most important part: in the past, the main question for these funds was how to generate higher returns. Today, in the current environment, it’s how to preserve what they have.

They’ve stopped building portfolios for a stable world and started building them for a world where conflicts, sanctions, and crises are simply part of the new normal.

The same logic applies to individual investors. Gold through allocated or bank-backed ownership programs, real assets, and diversification are more relevant today than ever.
